clauses.current_legal_basis: The held original (24 FR 5233) states no end. The only later instrument is Executive Order 12107 (44 FR 1055), whose section 2-101 amends and revises the order by substituting the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission, effective January 1, 1979; it keeps the order in force. The current-law:ecfr search (eCFR as of 2026-10-14) finds 5 CFR 351.502 (in effect on 2026-09-02), which still refers to cases under Executive Order 10826 pending resolution by OPM. 5 U.S.C. 3301, the codified derivation of the cited authority (5 U.S.C. 631; R.S. 1753), is held and current. Checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: Section 1 authorizes the Civil Service Commission to confer a benefit provided by an Executive order on an employee or former employee who became ineligible solely because an agency erred or overlooked making a timely determination or recommendation, only after the agency makes it and not retroactively; section 2 denies appeal rights against personnel actions effective before the agency was notified of the grant; section 3 revokes Executive Order 10535 of June 9, 1954, a one-time command complete in 1959. Executive Order 12107 section 2-101 amended the clause by substituting the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission and the Office for the Commission, effective January 1, 1979 under its section 2-404; before and after the change the authority is the same, and the amendment renames the actor. No held instrument revokes or supersedes the order, 5 CFR 351.502 still refers to cases under it, and its cited statutory authority survives in 5 U.S.C. 3301, so the clause is operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Read the whole order (24 FR 5233, signed 1959-06-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10826.txt): section 1 lets the Civil Service Commission confer a benefit under an Executive order on a Federal employee or former employee who met its requirements but became ineligible solely because an agency erred or overlooked making a timely determination or recommendation, only after the agency makes the required determination, with no action effective before the date it is taken; section 2 denies appeal rights against personnel actions made effective before the agency is notified of the grant; section 3 revokes Executive Order 10535 of June 9, 1954. The order has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes. later-events:ofr_catalog has 1 hit, the Office of the Federal Register note 'Amended by: EO 12107, December 28, 1978'; the held text of Executive Order 12107 (44 FR 1055, signed 1978-12-28) section 2-101 amends and revises each listed order, among them 10826, by substituting the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission, and section 2-404 makes the order effective January 1, 1979, so the amendment is recorded as a later event and does not end the order. current-law:usc has 0 hits (no U.S. Code note names the order). current-law:ecfr has 3 hits: 5 CFR 351.501 and 5 CFR 351.502, whose eCFR text (351.502 in effect on 2026-09-02) still refers to cases under Executive Order 10826 to correct certain administrative errors, pending resolution by OPM. The authority the order cites, section 2 of the Civil Service Act and Revised Statutes 1753 (5 U.S.C. 631), is the derivation of 5 U.S.C. 3301 (Pub. L. 89-554, 1966), held at jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s3301.txt, which still authorizes the President to prescribe regulations for admission into the civil service and was amended by Pub. L. 119-60 on December 18, 2025. The held-corpus search for the order's number found no revocation or supersession.

savings.reason: The order has no saving clause. Section 3 revoked Executive Order 10535 on issuance and no held source restores it. Section 2 limits only appeal rights in cases where a grant is made, which is part of the continuing grant of authority. The three bounded searches found no other residue or later instrument.
